nodes.body:
## Observed

Changing a playlist's `CrossfadeSeconds` while it is playing has no effect on the running
session. To hear the new value you must stop and restart playback:

```
# store-cli script --store TLV <file>
pl.CrossfadeSeconds = 5.0;   # was 2.0
ra.Stop = true;
ra.Play = true;              # only now does the 5 s overlap apply
```

Observed live on 2026-08-02 driving `/Home/Apartment/GuestsRoom/Audio` against a real
receiver: the property write alone changed nothing audible; the Stop/Play restarted the
track and the new overlap took effect.

## Expected

Editing the crossfade length should take effect at the *next track transition*, without
interrupting the track that is currently playing. Same ergonomics as a volume edit.

## Confirmed

- `PlaylistSource::new` (src/playlist.rs) computes `overlap_frames` ONCE at construction
  and moves it into the producer thread (`run_playlist(track_rx, overlap_frames, ...)`).
  Nothing can change it for the life of the source.
- The store side copies `CrossfadeSeconds` onto the `AudioSession` in `set_source`
  (data/frameworks/media/modules/media/air_zone_audio.sdl in the Store repo), i.e. at
  source-selection time only — a later edit to the playlist object does not republish.

## The two halves of a fix

**Store half — easy, has an exact precedent.** `SessionMember.on PropertyChanged(DesiredVolume)`
already bubbles a live member edit into `sync_session`. The same shape on the playlist's
`CrossfadeSeconds` (walking the same playlist → category → catalog hierarchy `set_source`
uses) would republish the desired doc on an edit.

**Daemon half — the substantive part.** `overlap_frames` has to become a live-readable
value (e.g. an `Arc<AtomicUsize>` the producer reads per transition) that the converge
loop updates when the desired doc changes, INSTEAD of a construction argument.

The trap to avoid: making the converge loop treat a changed `CrossfadeSeconds` as a
material source change would REOPEN the source and restart the current track — which is
worse than today's explicit Stop/Play, because it would happen silently on every edit.
The overlap must be updatable in place.

## Notes

- Same treatment probably wants to apply to `Shuffle` and `Loop`, which are baked in at
  the same point and have the same "edit does nothing until restart" behaviour. Worth
  confirming before scoping.
- Not a correctness bug; nothing is wrong or lost. This is an ergonomics improvement,
  raised by the user during the 2026-08-02 by-ear session.
Node **MP-305** in the Store repo's media port DAG (`docs/media-port-dag.md`) — part of the MP-3xx reliability band of the live-frontier mission.

## Daemon half shipped — `557a856`. Leaving open for the store half.

`overlap_frames` is now an `Arc<AtomicUsize>` the producer reads **once per transition**, so a republished doc with a new `CrossfadeSeconds` lands at the next track boundary and never disturbs the one now playing. That is what this issue calls "the substantive part".

**The trap you named is asserted, not trusted.** The update is applied in place and is deliberately not part of the source-change comparison; the test holds the ORIGINAL `Arc` across the edit and requires the session clock unchanged, the same cell still installed, and **zero RTSP methods** issued. Negative-controlled by actually implementing the trap — folding the crossfade into the source comparison reddens exactly the "must be KEPT" assertion.

Shape follows `skip_flag`: a defaulted `Source` method handing back the `Arc`, captured at open because the source is moved into the producer thread. A single file returns `None` — a crossfade means nothing there.

## Why the store half is not just "the easy one"

This issue describes it as easy with an exact precedent (`SessionMember.on PropertyChanged(DesiredVolume)` → `sync_session`). The precedent is real, but it does not transfer directly: a `SessionMember` **is a child of the session**, so `bubble` walks up two parents and calls `sync_session`. A playlist is not — it is a catalog object, and any number of sessions (or none) may be playing it.

So the bubble needs to answer "which sessions are playing THIS source?", and **the session does not record its source**. That is the missing link named in the title of Store [#105](https://github.com/yuvalrakavy/Store/issues/105) (MP-207: *"editing a Mix while it plays does nothing - no republish bubble, and AudioSession does not record its source"*).

Same prerequisite, same fix. Doing them together avoids building the lookup twice, and #105's Mix case is the harder one — a Mix edit has to reach sessions playing the Mix, which is where the traversal actually needs designing.

**In the meantime:** the value is live the moment ANYTHING republishes the desired doc, so a member edit or a re-select already carries a new crossfade through without a Stop/Play.

## Closed — both halves shipped

**Daemon half** — airzoned `557a856`. `overlap_frames` is an `Arc<AtomicUsize>` the producer reads once per transition, so a new value lands at the next track boundary and never disturbs the one playing. The trap this issue names is asserted rather than trusted: the test holds the original `Arc` across the edit and requires the session clock unchanged, the same cell installed, and **zero RTSP methods** — negative-controlled by actually implementing the trap.

**Store half** — Store `2b54d461`. This is where the issue's estimate was off, and usefully so.

It called the store half *"easy, has an exact precedent"* — `SessionMember.on PropertyChanged(DesiredVolume)` bubbling to `sync_session`. The precedent is real but does not transfer: a `SessionMember` **is a child of the session**, so its bubble walks up two parents. A playlist is a catalog object, and any number of sessions may be playing it — so the bubble first has to answer *"which sessions are playing me?"*, and the session did not record its source.

That is the model decision Store #105 identified, and it had to be made first: `AudioSession.SourceRef` now records the origin, and the reverse index answers the question directly — not the scan #105 rejected as *"fine with three sessions and badly with thirty"*.

## Why the parameter edit is safe, stated because it is the load-bearing part

A Crossfade/Shuffle/Loop edit leaves the expansion **byte-identical**, so the daemon keeps the session (it hard-cuts only on a changed source list) and the daemon half applies the new value live. The two halves interlock exactly there.

A Mix **membership** change does alter `Sources` and would restart the current track by that same rule — which is why #105's own case is deliberately not wired to this yet. It is a UX decision, not an implementation detail.

nodes.title: CrossfadeSeconds (and Shuffle/Loop) only take effect after a Stop/Play

nodes.body:
Stopping playback and starting it again on the SAME speaker leaves the receiver wedged:
you hear roughly half a second of audio and then silence, while the daemon believes it is
playing normally.

Reproduced three times in a row on 2026-08-02 against a real Yamaha receiver
(`00A0DE91CBCB@BZm Yuval O`, 10.0.2.158:1024, RAOP port 1024).

## Observed

Drive a room's `RoomAudio` (Store side), with a local `.m3u` playlist source:

```
ra.Stop = true;
# ~3 seconds later
ra.Play = true;
```

Daemon log:

```
[engine] member m33558669: stop — fading out over 22050 frames, retiring
[engine] reap-before-connect: tearing down a member still retiring on 10.0.2.158
[engine] member m33558669: connected — receiver Audio-Latency = 4096 frames (~92 ms)
[airzoned] decode: ffmpeg fallback for /Volumes/Media/Music/.../03 ....wma
```

Result: about half a second of audio out of the speaker, then silence. The daemon stays
healthy — a stack sample (`sample <pid> 4`) shows every stage alive and paced:

- `send_loop` (engine/member.rs:403) mostly in its pacing sleep, periodically inside
  `AlacStream::encode` (member.rs:383) — i.e. still encoding and sending RTP
- `engine::producer::produce` (engine/producer.rs:88) in its pacing sleep, pulling on schedule
- `run_playlist` producer parked in `Packetizer::push` (playlist.rs:381) — frame channel full
- `run_fetcher` parked in `tx.send` (playlist.rs:136) — track channel full

Both are normal backpressure: the pipeline is full and moving at real-time rate. The RTSP
TCP connection to 10.0.2.158:1024 stays ESTABLISHED and the RTP sockets stay open. Nothing
is logged as an error.

The Store-side observed state also still reads `Transport = 4` (playing) throughout, so a
panel would show "playing" over silence.

## The control arm (this is what makes it a real finding, not a one-off)

With NO retiring member to collide with, the identical Play works and audio plays normally:

```
1. clear the session (Stop)
2. SIGTERM the daemon      -> graceful RTSP TEARDOWN, exits cleanly in ~2 s
3. wait ~12 s
4. start a fresh daemon
5. Play ONCE (no Stop before it)
```

Log shows a clean connect with `reap-before-connect` count = 0, and the user confirmed
audio plays. So the discriminating variable is the presence of a retiring member on the
same speaker at connect time, not the receiver, the network, or the source.

## Expected

Stop followed by Play on the same speaker should play normally. This is the most basic
thing a wall panel does, and it is on the M1 "tap the wall, music plays" path.

## Confirmed

- A retiring member deliberately KEEPS STREAMING to its speaker until reaped —
  `engine/member.rs` synthesizes a silence packet when the ring runs dry while `retiring`,
  with the rationale that "a STALLED stream wedges the receiver's session ... which is the
  stop→replay-after-the-grace wedge". So during the retire grace there is a live RTP stream
  to that speaker.
- `reap-before-connect` exists precisely to tear that down before a new member connects,
  and it DOES fire (see the log above) — yet the wedge still occurs. So either the teardown
  is not complete before the new SETUP/RECORD reaches the receiver, or the receiver needs
  longer than the reap takes to release the session.

## Hypotheses — UNVERIFIED, do not trust

- The reap and the new connect race: the reap issues TEARDOWN but does not wait for the
  receiver to actually release before the new session's ANNOUNCE/SETUP/RECORD arrives, so
  the receiver briefly holds two sessions and ends up rendering neither.
- The receiver may need a settling interval after TEARDOWN before it will accept a new
  session cleanly; if so the fix is to make reap-before-connect synchronous plus a small
  enforced gap, rather than best-effort.
- Not checked: whether the same wedge occurs when the new member targets a DIFFERENT
  speaker than the retiring one (which would separate "receiver session state" from
  "daemon-side member bookkeeping").

Reproduce first and let the evidence lead; do not assume the above.

## Notes

- Pre-existing: the retire logic predates the 2026-08-02 commits (gapless decode-ahead,
  ffmpeg fallback, ALAC buffer fix, graceful shutdown). Those commits are not the cause,
  though the added decode CPU load during connect may widen the window.
- Related design context: this is spec risk #7 "cross-session speaker contention" in
  `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-19-airzone-player-design.md` (Store repo).
- Also relevant: the Store-side observed `Transport` never changes, so there is no honest
  transport feedback for this failure. Spec section 11.1 requires exactly that
  ("never a blank now-playing screen"). A fix should surface the failure, not only avoid it.

Grounded the issue's claims against the code before designing a fix. **The leading hypothesis in
the original report is WRONG** and should not be worked from.

## What the original report got wrong

It assumed the receiver REFUSES the new session ("interruption not allowed") because the reap
races the new connect. It does not. In the captured log the new connect **succeeds** — it
returns `Audio-Latency = 4096 frames (~92 ms)`, which only comes back from a completed
RTSP handshake. So the receiver accepts the session and then fails to render it. That is a
different bug with a different fix, and the reap/connect race is not it.

## What is now confirmed (traced to code, not comments)

- `RetiringPool` logic is correct and unit-tested against a mock: `park` evicts a prior member on
  the same IP, `reap` removes and tears down by IP, `sweep` respects deadlines (`engine/retire.rs`).
- reap-before-connect really is ordered correctly and synchronously on the real path:
  `engine/mod.rs:193` calls `self.retiring.reap(addr.ip())` immediately before
  `MemberSender::connect_and_spawn(...)`, same thread, sequential.
- `MemberSender::teardown` (`engine/member.rs:256`) is fully synchronous: clears `running`, joins
  the send/timing/control threads, then issues `rtsp.teardown()`.
- `Session::new` (`engine/mod.rs:139-153`) mints a FRESH `SessionClock` per session, so a genuinely
  new session cannot inherit a stale RTP timeline.

So every element the original report suspected is behaving as designed.

## New hypothesis — UNVERIFIED

The Store reuses the SAME session name across a stop/start: both the wedged run and the clean run
used `/Services/AirZone/m33558669` (the id derives from the RoomAudio object, not the play
episode). In the first occurrence the trigger was two back-to-back micro-transactions with no gap:

```
ra.Stop = true;
ra.Play = true;
```

If the retained desired doc is cleared and re-published within milliseconds, the daemon's converge
loop may never observe the session as ABSENT — so it would keep the SAME `Session` (same clock,
same ring, same producer wiring) and merely see the member set change: remove -> retire -> re-add.
The new member then starts at `clock.target_now() + JOIN_LEAD_PKTS` against a ring whose contents
and producer state belong to the previous play episode. That is consistent with the observed
symptom (a fraction of a second of audio, then silence) in a way that "the receiver refused us"
is not.

Note the clean run that WORKED had a full daemon restart between stop and play, which destroys the
Session unambiguously — so the two arms differ in session lifetime, not only in retire state. That
weakens the original "retiring member collides" reading further.

## How to discriminate (not yet done)

Instrument rather than reason: log session create/destroy with the clock's `start_instant` and the
ring's committed seq, then reproduce both arms —

1. `Stop; Play` back-to-back (no gap) — the original trigger.
2. `Stop`, wait past `RetireGrace` (5 s), then `Play` — retire fully drained, same session id.
3. `Stop`, restart the daemon, `Play` — known-good control.

If (2) plays cleanly and (1) does not, the cause is session reuse / timeline, not the retiring
member. If (2) also wedges, the retiring member is back in scope.

Not yet run: reproducing needs a real receiver and a listener, since there is no programmatic
signal for "the speaker is actually making sound" — worth adding one (the observed `Transport`
never leaves "playing" through the whole failure, which is the separate honest-feedback gap noted
in the report).

## ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED — mid-fade teardown

Isolated by a four-arm A/B against the real receiver on 2026-08-02, with instrumentation added
to make session/member lifecycle visible (`[player] session=… CREATED/KEPT/STOPPING/CLEAR`,
`[engine] member … JOINED/REMOVED` with ring lag and live seq).

| Arm | `LeaveFade` | Stop→Play gap | Fade state when reaped | Audio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 500 ms | 0 (back-to-back) | **still ramping** | **SILENT** (reproduced twice) |
| 1 | **0** | 0 (back-to-back) | nothing to interrupt | plays |
| 1b | 500 ms | 2 s | complete | plays |
| 2 | 500 ms | 9 s | complete | plays |

Exactly one variable separates a wedge from a clean replay: **whether the outgoing member's
fade-out envelope had finished when `reap-before-connect` tore it down.** Setting `LeaveFade = 0`
makes the identical back-to-back sequence work, which rules out every timing explanation that is
not the fade — same code path, same near-zero TEARDOWN→SETUP gap, same everything else.

`reap-before-connect` issues the RTSP TEARDOWN while the receiver still holds real, non-silent
audio queued from the in-progress fade. The immediately-following SETUP for the new session then
leaves the receiver accepting the session (the handshake succeeds and returns
`Audio-Latency = 4096 frames`) but never rendering it.

## Both earlier hypotheses are dead

- "The receiver refuses the second session as an interruption" — no: the handshake SUCCEEDS.
- "The daemon reuses a stale session / stale timeline" — no: the instrumentation shows a fresh
  `Session` with a new id and a new clock every time (`CREATED`, `session_age≈1.4s`,
  `ring_lag≈123`, i.e. a full ~1 s of program buffered at join). The daemon-side pipeline is
  healthy and IDENTICAL in the wedged and the working arms.
- Also dead: "the TEARDOWN→SETUP gap is the variable". Arms 1 and 1b have the same ~0 gap and
  differ in outcome.

## The underlying defect is an unenforced invariant

`engine/member.rs`'s retiring path synthesizes silence once the ring runs dry, on the stated
assumption that "the gain is already faded to 0". Nothing enforces that: `Session::remove` calls
`snd.request_stop(leave_fade_frames)` and then IMMEDIATELY `retiring.park(...)`, so a member can
be parked — and reaped — while its envelope has barely started to ramp. The comment describes an
invariant the code does not maintain.

## Fix shapes (not yet chosen)

1. **Wait for the fade at reap.** Record a `fade_done_at` alongside `reap_at` in `RetiringMember`;
   `reap()` waits until that instant before `shutdown()`. Cost is paid ONLY on a same-speaker
   collision (the rare path), bounded by `LeaveFade`. Smallest change that addresses the actual
   cause.
2. **Make the invariant true at park time.** Do not consider a member parked until its fade has
   played out. Cleanest conceptually — it makes the documented assumption true for every consumer
   (`reap`, `sweep`, `drain`) — but pays the fade latency on every removal, not just collisions.
3. **Warm reuse** (already named in `retire.rs`'s module doc as the M1 seam). Do not
   teardown+setup at all: reactivate the parked member for the new session (FLUSH + fade-in).
   Eliminates the RTSP churn entirely and gives the best UX (no gap at all), but is the largest
   change.

Recommendation: (1) now, (3) as the M1 evolution. (2) is tempting but taxes the common path to fix
a rare one.

## Note for whoever implements this

There is still no programmatic signal for "the speaker is actually rendering" — every arm above
had to be judged by ear, and the Store-side observed `Transport` read "playing" throughout all of
them, including the silent ones. That is the honest-feedback gap from spec section 11.1 and it is
what made this take four arms instead of one. Worth fixing alongside, or this class of bug stays
ear-only forever.

Fixed in 3df4b60 and verified on the real receiver.

`park()` now records `fade_done_at`, and a shared `shutdown_after_fade` helper refuses to tear a
member down before its fade has played out — applied on every teardown path (`reap`, `park`
eviction, `sweep`, `drain`), capped at 2 s so a pathological config cannot stall the converge
thread.

Verification, both arms:

* The reproduction in the report no longer reproduces. The identical back-to-back
  `ra.Stop = true; ra.Play = true` with `LeaveFade = 500 ms` — which produced ~0.5 s of audio then
  silence three separate times — now plays through, confirmed by ear.
* The mechanism is observably firing:
  `reap-before-connect: tearing down a member still retiring on 10.0.2.158 (waiting 366.482375ms
  for its fade to finish first)`, followed by a clean connect and rejoin.
* Four unit tests, negative-controlled: with the wait disabled, exactly the three that pin the
  rule go red; the fourth pins the opposite edge so a finished fade cannot introduce a needless
  stall.

Left deliberately open as separate work, both noted in the thread: there is still no programmatic
signal for "the speaker is actually rendering" (the Store-side observed `Transport` read "playing"
throughout every silent arm), which is the spec section 11.1 honest-feedback obligation and is what
made this take four hardware arms to isolate.

nodes.title: reap-before-connect tears down a member mid-fade, wedging the receiver

nodes.body:
## Observed

Raising `LeaveFade` in `{Root}/Config` from 500 ms to 4500 ms produces an ABRUPT stop, not a
4.5 s fade. Verified live on 2026-08-02 against a real receiver.

The config round-trips correctly and the engine believes it is honouring it:

```
[airzoned] config applied: preroll=1000ms silence_lead=1022ms join_fade=750ms
           leave_fade=4500ms retire_grace=5000ms volume=-8dB
[engine] member m33558669: stop — fading out over 198450 frames, retiring
```

198450 frames is exactly 4500 ms x 44.1, so the envelope really is armed for 4.5 s. What the
listener hears is a hard cut.

## Expected

`LeaveFade = 4500` should produce an audible 4.5 s musical fade-out. Failing that, the config
lane should refuse or clamp the value with a warning rather than accept it and silently degrade
to a cut.

## Confirmed

The fade can only be as long as the audio still buffered in the ring when the session's producer
is dropped at Stop, and that is ~0.5 s:

- `engine/mod.rs`: `PREROLL_LEAD_PKTS = 64` (~0.5 s) — the producer keeps the ring filled only to
  `clock.target_now() + lead`, and `produce()` paces itself with `thread::sleep(BURST_PERIOD)`.
  A stack sample during playback showed the producer 3140/3151 samples inside that sleep, i.e.
  it stays at its small lead and never runs far ahead.
- `engine/mod.rs`: `RING_CAPACITY_PKTS = 768` (~6 s). The ring is big enough for a long fade; it
  simply is never filled that far ahead, because the producer is paced, not eager.
- `engine/member.rs` (the `retiring` + `ReadOutcome::NotYetCommitted` arm): once the ring runs
  dry the retiring member synthesizes `[[0.0; 2]; FPP]` silence, with the comment "the gain is
  already faded to 0". That assumption is TRUE for a 500 ms fade and FALSE for anything longer
  than the producer's lead.

So the previous default was not arbitrary: `LeaveFade = 500 ms` matched `PREROLL_LEAD_PKTS`
almost exactly, which is why the fade completed to zero inside the buffered audio. At 4500 ms
you get ~0.5 s of fade (full down to roughly 89% gain — inaudible as a fade) followed by ~4 s
of silence.

## Two defects, not one

1. **The engine cannot honour a fade longer than the producer lead.** The stop path drops the
   session producer immediately, so there is no further real audio to fade.
2. **The config lane accepts the value anyway and degrades silently.** Nothing warns, and the
   log line ("fading out over 198450 frames") actively suggests it worked. Whatever is decided
   about (1), the silent degradation is its own bug.

## Fix shape (not yet designed — needs a decision)

The correct fix is to keep the session producer alive through the fade: at Stop, arm the
envelope, keep producing real audio until the fade has fully played out, and only then drop the
producer and enter the silence/retire phase. The retire phase's "gain is already faded to 0"
comment then becomes true by construction instead of by coincidence.

Interaction to check before implementing: `RetireGrace` (currently 5000 ms) must remain greater
than `LeaveFade`, and a longer fade means a retiring member streams to its speaker for longer —
which widens the window for the stop-then-play wedge in #2. These two issues should probably be
designed together.

Cheap interim mitigation if the full fix is deferred: clamp `LeaveFade` to the producer lead at
config-apply time and WARN when clamping, so the value cannot silently lie.

## Notes

Raised by the user during the 2026-08-02 by-ear session ("Stop fade-out should also be 4-5
seconds"), then reproduced and root-caused. `LeaveFade` has been reverted to 500 ms in the
meantime so the short fade works correctly.

Correction to my own report: **I cited the wrong constant.**

The producer lead is `PRODUCTION_AHEAD_PKTS = 128` (~1 s) — `engine/mod.rs:38`, "Packets the
producer keeps written ahead of live", and it is the value actually passed to `spawn_producer`
at `player.rs:215`.

`PREROLL_LEAD_PKTS = 64` (~0.5 s), which the report cited, is a DIFFERENT quantity: "Packets a
joiner starts ahead of live", i.e. the new member's join offset. I matched it by name
resemblance instead of checking which constant the call site passes.

What changes:

* The producer lead is **~1 s**, not ~0.5 s.
* The claim that `LeaveFade = 500 ms` "matched `PREROLL_LEAD_PKTS` almost exactly, which is why
  the fade completed" is wrong. The real reason a 500 ms fade works is simply that it fits
  comfortably inside the ~1 s of audio the producer keeps buffered ahead.

What does NOT change: the defect. A 4500 ms fade still cannot be honoured, because the producer
is dropped at Stop and only ~1 s of real audio remains in the ring — so ~1 s of fade is followed
by ~3.5 s of synthesized silence. The fix shape (keep the producer alive through the fade) and
the interim mitigation (clamp `LeaveFade` to the lead and WARN) are unaffected.

Fixed in 1dd554a and verified on hardware — a 4.5 s fade now sounds like a fade ("stopped nicely").

The producer is DETACHED at stop rather than dropped with the session: `stop_session` takes its
handle, marks the session `producer_detached` so `Drop` leaves it alone, and hands it to a stopper
that clears the running flag after the fade and joins it. The parked members hold their own ring
`Arc` and clock `Copy`, so the ring keeps being filled once the session object is gone.

Because the member drains in real time and the producer fills in real time, the ring never has to
hold the whole fade — so the ceiling on fade length is gone entirely, not merely raised. It is now
bounded only by `RetireGrace`, which must stay greater than `LeaveFade`.

Verification: `LeaveFade = 4500` -> `CREATED … leave_fade_frames=198450` ->
`producer LINGERING 4.5s so the fade has real audio` -> a real 4.5 s fade by ear. Afterwards the
daemon is back to 2 threads at 0% CPU with the producer stopped and joined, so the detached producer
does not leak.

Also corrected here: the report originally cited `PREROLL_LEAD_PKTS` (~0.5 s) as the producer lead.
The lead is `PRODUCTION_AHEAD_PKTS` = 128 (~1 s), confirmed empirically by the new instrumentation
(`ring_lag≈123..127` at join).

Two follow-ups deliberately left open:

* A replay issued DURING a long fade now waits for that fade before the new session can connect,
  since the reap must not tear down mid-fade (see #2). Safe, but at 4.5 s it reads as an
  unresponsive panel. Cutting the fade short on an explicit replay is the likely answer; it is a UX
  decision, not a code one.
* The "clamp and warn" mitigation is no longer needed for the ring-capacity reason, but a
  `LeaveFade >= RetireGrace` config is still nonsense and is not currently rejected.

nodes.title: LeaveFade longer than the producer lead (~0.5s) degrades silently to an abrupt cut

nodes.body: > **Status 2026-10-23:** still open, checked against `7b4623f`. Note: the daemon now *sends* `SET_PARAMETER progress` (Store #88 / MP-107) as a sender-to-receiver push; that is **not** the signal this issue wants, and nothing is read back. The unbuilt candidate is `GET_PARAMETER progress` (see the `timing_loop` doc, `src/engine/member.rs:862-876`). The two instrument defects in the 2026-08-02 comment are at `connect_attempt_begins` (`src/engine/mod.rs:549-559`): it logs before the handshake, and formats with `{since:?}` (Debug units). They could be split off as a small self-contained task. ## Observed The daemon cannot tell whether a receiver is ACTUALLY RENDERING. Every local stage can look perfectly healthy — RTSP socket ESTABLISHED, send loop encoding on schedule, ring full, member joined — while the room is silent. This is not hypothetical: it is what made the mid-fade wedge (#2) take four hardware A/B arms and a listener to isolate. Throughout every silent arm the Store-side observed `Transport` read "Playing". ## What was tried, and what it does NOT cover 2ae3113 added a receiver heartbeat: `timing_loop` records when the receiver last asked us for timing, and a member that goes quiet past `TIMING_SILENCE_UNHEALTHY_MS` (8 s, chosen from a measured ~2.0–2.5 s request period) publishes observed `Failed`. That catches a receiver that is GONE — powered off, standby, off the network, crashed — which was previously invisible and is a real gain. **It does not catch a receiver that is present but not rendering.** Established by experiment, not assumed: the wedge was deliberately re-induced by disabling the fade-wait, the room was silent for 30 s, and the timing requests kept arriving the whole time. The threshold was never crossed. A heartbeat proves liveness; liveness is not playback. ## Expected A signal that distinguishes "rendering" from "connected but silent", so this failure class is diagnosable from the logs and the Store instead of from a person in the room. Spec section 11.1 requires honest transport feedback and is currently only partly met. ## Hypotheses — UNVERIFIED * **RTSP `GET_PARAMETER progress`** is the most promising: RAOP receivers report a playback position for scrub bars. Polling it and checking that it ADVANCES would answer the question directly. Unverified: whether this particular Yamaha implements it, what it returns while wedged (it may report a frozen position, which is exactly the signal we want — or it may not respond at all), and what the polling cost is. * Retransmit requests are NOT a candidate: they only appear on packet loss, so their absence proves nothing. Verify against real hardware before designing around any of this — the heartbeat idea looked obviously right too, and was wrong. ## Why it matters beyond debugging Once this exists, the wedge class (and any future variant) fails LOUDLY. The panel can then honour the section 11.1 contract — "never a blank now-playing screen" — and offer a recovery instead of showing "Playing" over silence. --- ### Position in the media-port DAG **Depends on** — must land first - yuvalrakavy/Store#72 — **MP-004** · ✔ done **Blocks** — waiting on this - _nothing_ Generated from [`docs/media-port-dag.md`](https://github.com/yuvalrakavy/Store/blob/main/docs/media-port-dag.md) — the DAG is the source of truth; edit it there and re-run scripts/dag-sync-issues.py. Edges point from dependency to dependent.

The pre-merge gate on `feat/m3-streaming-sources` sharpened why this matters, judging the new logging as a requirement rather than decoration.

That branch added the two intervals that bracket a wedge — silence→TEARDOWN and TEARDOWN→SETUP — so that a recurrence produces numbers instead of another uncontrolled A/B. But **neither line records whether that instance actually wedged.** A field recurrence therefore yields two intervals and no outcome, and correlating them still needs a human ear or `scripts/listen.sh`.

That is this issue: there is no rendering signal. `unhealthy_members` explicitly cannot serve as one — the timing heartbeat kept arriving through 30 s of deliberately induced silence, so liveness is not playback.

The candidate the code already names is RTSP `GET_PARAMETER progress`, polled for advancement. If that advances only while the receiver is really rendering, it converts every one of these logs from "here are two intervals" into "here are two intervals AND whether it worked", which is what makes the data self-interpreting.

Two smaller instrument defects found alongside, worth folding in whenever this is picked up:

* The SETUP-side line fires *before* `connect_and_spawn`, which does TCP connect + `auth_setup` + ANNOUNCE first — so the reported gap understates the true TEARDOWN→SETUP interval by an unmeasured handshake, and nothing logs that handshake's duration.
* The intervals print with `Duration`'s `Debug`, so units vary between runs (`950ms`, `1.02s`, `9.974258042s`). Hostile to sweeping across runs, and inconsistent with the daemon's own `... {} ms` convention.
Node **MP-304** in the Store repo's media port DAG (`docs/media-port-dag.md`) — part of the MP-3xx reliability band of the live-frontier mission.

nodes.title: No signal for 'the receiver is actually rendering' — heartbeat proves liveness, not playback

nodes.body:
Pre-merge gate on `origin/main..2ae3113` (three fresh-context finders, 2026-08-02) found five defects
that are ONE root cause: the teardown wait is ESTIMATED from wall-clock deadlines and its ownership is
split between two actors. Filing them together because patching them separately is what produced them.

**This surface has now been revised twice and a gate found holes both times.** That is the signal to
change the shape, not to add a third set of rules.

## Confirmed defects (all traced to code)

**A. `reap` silently no-ops while `sweep` owns the entry, so SETUP races an in-flight TEARDOWN.**
`sweep()` (`engine/retire.rs`) removes the entry from the map and THEN runs `shutdown_after_fade` with
the lock released. In that window the entry is absent-but-alive, so a converge-thread `reap(ip)` finds
`None` and returns immediately, and `connect_and_spawn` issues ANNOUNCE/SETUP while the old member's
TEARDOWN has not been sent. Window ≈1.05 s (send-thread join ≤50 ms + timing and control joins ≤500 ms
each, then TEARDOWN), starting at `park + retire_grace` ±250 ms of reaper tick. The module doc claims
this cannot happen; that claim is true of map ownership and false of the invariant it exists to protect.
Consequence: receiver refuses, `add` marks the member `pending`, and NOTHING retries when
`mdns_realm` is unset (`retry_unresolved`'s only caller is the mDNS branch) — silent dead room while
`reconcile` publishes `Playing`.

**B. The wait blocks the converge thread AFTER the new session's clock has started, dropping audio.**
In `reconcile`, `create_session` starts the clock and the producer (writing from seq 0), and only then
does `converge → add → reap → sleep`. The join cursor is computed after the sleep
(`clock.target_now(now) + JOIN_LEAD_PKTS`), so everything written during it is skipped — no `Evicted`,
no log line. With `LeaveFade=4500` and a replay 0.5 s after stop, ≈3.5 s of the track is dropped
(worse for Playlist/Stream sources, which have no silence lead). The daemon also processes no desired
docs and runs no health check for that whole window.

**C. The wait covers the fade being SENT, not RENDERED.** `fade_done_at = park + leave_fade` is the
instant the last faded packet goes on the wire. The receiver renders it `RTP_PREROLL` (1 s) plus its
own Audio-Latency later. `record()` MEASURES that Audio-Latency, logs it, and discards it. So any
replay in `(fade_done_at, fade_done_at + preroll + audio_latency)` still tears down mid-render. Note
the four-arm A/B arm that worked used a 2 s gap ≈ preroll + fade — consistent with pipeline drain,
not fade completion, being the operative mechanism.

**D. `LeaveFade >= RetireGrace` inverts the bound and re-arms the original wedge.** `until =
min(fade_done_at, reap_at)`. Both are free admin knobs over `{Root}/Config` with no validation. With
`LeaveFade=6000, RetireGrace=5000` (default grace is 5000, and the producer-linger was built for a
4500 fade — 500 ms of headroom), `sweep`'s due-filter checks only `reap_at`, so at the tick where
`now >= reap_at` the remaining wait is ZERO and TEARDOWN fires a full second before the fade ends, on
EVERY natural stop. A second path reaches the same place without misconfiguration: any fade above
`MAX_FADE_WAIT` (10 s) is truncated by the cap. The claim that the producer-linger "removes the
ceiling on how long a fade can be" is therefore false past ~10 s — the linger is uncapped and the
teardown wait is capped, and the teardown wins.

**E. `sweep` acts on a stale due-set.** The due list is computed under one lock and each entry removed
under a second, with no re-check of `reap_at`. A `park` during the first teardown can install a fresh
member at a later index, which is then reaped honouring its fade but discarding its grace.

## Proposed shape — stop estimating, observe

The member already emits `StopComplete` when its envelope reaches zero, and `record()` already learns
the receiver's real Audio-Latency. The teardown condition should be "the fade has been RENDERED" =
`StopComplete` + `RTP_PREROLL` + that measured latency — not a guessed sleep on the converge thread.

That collapses A, C, D and E into one mechanism and deletes `MAX_FADE_WAIT` entirely. B is independent
and is fixed by performing the reap BEFORE `create_session`, so any wait precedes the clock start.

Also unresolved and needing a decision: a replay issued during a long fade must either wait it out
(unresponsive) or cut it short (needs the "receiver holds no real audio" guarantee re-established some
other way — force gain to zero, then drain). This is a UX call.

## Test gaps to close in the same pass

Every existing fade-wait test calls `reap()` immediately after `park()`, never through the natural
sweep-at-deadline path, and never with `fade > grace` — so none of them can catch D. They also assert
only LOWER bounds: dropping `fade_done_at` from the `min` makes every reap block for the full grace,
and the suite went from 0.36 s to 20 s while still reporting green. Upper-bound assertions needed.

The pre-merge gate found that `restart-daemon.sh` waited 3s for the old daemon and launched regardless, while a normal shutdown takes 6-16s. Two daemons overlapped routinely; the newcomer's retiring pool is empty (different process) so it SETUPs over the incumbent's live session, which then receives the incumbent's TEARDOWN and goes silent — indistinguishable from this issue at the speaker.

**The settle A/B was run through that script.** So the '2s still wedges' arm is contaminated, and the apparent gap threshold in (2s, 15s] is suspiciously exactly the old daemon's shutdown budget. Those arms must be re-run on the fixed script (`658aee7`) before anything is concluded from them.

What survives: the ~1ms replay wedged with the drain provably satisfied, inside ONE process, no restart involved. This issue is real; only the gap-length story is in doubt.

nodes.title: Redesign the teardown wait: observe render completion instead of estimating deadlines (5 gate findings, one root cause)
